items.decision: The diagnose skill never fixes. It takes in the bug, checks that it is real, compares it with the specs, reproduces it, finds the root cause and ends with a proposed fix. It stays usable on its own.
items.evidence: Your words: "afk:diagnose should not fix, all of that intake, verify the bug, reproduce, specs check, etc should be part of diagnose ... and propose a fix" and "confirm afk:diagnose could be used standalone".

items.decision: The fix skill does the fix: it runs diagnose, gets approval, fixes, verifies (re-testing after the fix is part of this), takes proof, creates and writes the merge request, and updates the ticket.
items.evidence: Your words: "afk:fix do the fix, which include afk:diagnose, verification, take proof, create + write MR, update JIRA" and "re-testing after the fix is the verification step which should be done in afk:fix".

items.decision: Behaviour shared between skills lives in one markdown file that skills point at. A new skill is created only when a human must be able to run it.
items.evidence: Your words: "do not create a skill if not needed (eg don't need it to be invocable). create just a markdown and refer to it only instead".

items.decision: The bug skill retires. The to-ticket skill publishes bug and ad-hoc tickets instead, adjusted for that use.
items.evidence: Your words: "afk:bug I think we can retire" and "instead of afk:bug, afk:to-ticket can publish the tickets, so we need adjustments here".

items.decision: The fix asks for human approval before it changes anything, unless an explicit instruction or approval was given beforehand.
items.evidence: Your words: "seeking approval is the default behavior, unless explicit instruction or approval was given beforehand".

items.decision: A complex bug, one with no obvious fix, or one that needs a product owner's call goes to a grilling session instead of a direct fix.
items.evidence: Your words: "for a more complex one, not obvious solution, or require product owner call, etc, then grilling would be needed".

items.decision: Diagnose leaves a test that fails because of the bug, as proof that it reproduced the bug. The fix makes that test pass.

items.decision: Diagnose ends with one of five verdicts: a real bug with an obvious fix, a real bug with several possible fixes, a gap in the specs, works as specified, or cannot reproduce.
items.evidence: Proposed on 2026-10-09; not objected to, under your standing rule. Reopen it here if that reading is wrong.

items.decision: The fix has two modes: in place, when another skill calls it inside its own branch and that skill ships the change; and standalone, when it ships the change itself.
items.evidence: Proposed on 2026-10-09; not objected to, under your standing rule. Reopen it here if that reading is wrong.

items.decision: Starting a hands-off run counts as approval given beforehand. Inside such a run the fix follows the decision protocol: it goes ahead on a change that is easy to undo and stops for the human otherwise.
items.evidence: Proposed on 2026-10-09; consistent with your rule on approval given beforehand. Reopen it here if that reading is wrong.

items.decision: The diagnose and fix path covers bugs only; to-ticket also files ad-hoc enhancement tickets. Bugs can be of any size; an enhancement is never small and always goes through a proper grill.
items.evidence: Your answer: B, with the note "bugs can be of any size. enhancement can never be small, it is at least medium and always need careful consideration, so proper grilling is always necessary".

items.decision: A grill that a bug was sent to ends with a size call: back to the fix skill when the bug is still small, into the full chain when it is not.

items.decision: A standalone diagnosis runs in its own worktree off the base branch and keeps the failing test there on a local branch named in the diagnosis file.
Mid-task capture is a ticket filed with to-ticket from a written description; diagnosis and fix run later.
The fix keeps escape analysis, spec reconciliation and the workflow lesson.
The removal is complete only when no reference to the bug skill remains outside the changelog and the setup audit passes.
A ticket filed by the old pipeline is fixed by passing its key to the fix; no migration.
The developer settings the bug skill documents keep their names and meaning; only their documentation moves.
Bugs left in flight by the old pipeline get a way out through the release notes.
As a developer, I run diagnose with a ticket key or a description and get a diagnosis file with a verdict and a fix proposal; no product code changes.

As a developer, I run fix on a bug: it diagnoses, I approve or steer the proposal, it fixes test-first, runs every tier, collects proof, files or updates the ticket and opens a ready merge request with a reviewer.
As a developer whose diagnosis finds several possible fixes or a spec gap, I am sent to a grill that ends with a size call: back to the fix, or into the full chain.
As a developer whose diagnosis finds the behaviour works as specified, the fix stops; to change the behaviour I file an enhancement ticket with to-ticket, which then needs a grill.
As a developer whose diagnosis cannot reproduce the bug, I get what was tried and what is needed, and with my approval it is posted on the ticket.
As a developer, I file a bug or an ad-hoc enhancement ticket with to-ticket from a diagnosis file or a written description, including mid-task.
As a developer upgrading the plugin, the release notes tell me the bug skill is gone, diagnose no longer fixes, and how to clean up what the old pipeline left.
A bug found inside a bigger job gets no diagnosis; the caller fixes it inline, as today.
A check that fails on code the run just wrote is fixed inside the build loop with today's one targeted retry.
A failure that passes on re-run is reported as flaky with both runs and never fixed by changing product code.
A bug reported by a human testing the feature branch gets the full diagnosis, lands in place on the feature branch, and that human approves it.
One spinoff ticket covers the medium and large lanes and carries the known limit; filed at the end of this grill.
Still red after the retry: an in-place fix with no diagnosis step; regression test, tiers, escape analysis and the workflow lesson still run.
A review finding naming a defect: an in-place fix with no diagnosis step; a wrong finding is disputed in the settle loop.
An adversary finding: an in-place fix with no diagnosis step; its reproduction becomes the permanent test.
A red feature smoke gate: an in-place fix per failing scenario, with no diagnosis step.
An in-place fix returns today's outcomes and no diagnosis verdict; the works-as-specified outcome is dropped.
As an agent implementing a feature, I fix a stubborn red check or a defect finding in place with no diagnosis, approve it under the decision protocol, and ship it with the feature.

A defect outside the slice that blocks it gets a diagnosis, full or light, so its ticket stands alone with evidence and proof; it is fixed on its own branch and merge request linked to that ticket, the same fix goes on the feature branch, and both merges stay with the human.
